summary: Douglas Allen is a philosophy and religious studies scholar. He studied at Yale, Banaras Hindu, and Vanderbilt universities. His posts include Southern Illinois University Carbondale, Central Connecticut State, and the University of Maine, where he became Professor Emeritus in 2020.

Douglas Gildow is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Princeton University, studying under doctoral supervisor Stephen F. Teiser and supervisor Qi Zhou.

Douglas L. Berger works in philosophy, Sinology, and Indology. He has held positions at Southern Illinois University Carbondale (attested 2007–2014) and Leiden University (attested 2026), and served as General Editor for Dimensions of Asian Spirituality (attested 2012).

Douglas Ober is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington under Charles Keyes and others, and earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Harjot Oberoi.

Douglas Osto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and completed his PhD under Ulrich Pagel at SOAS University of London (~1999–2004). In 2005, he became a Senior Lecturer at Massey University.

Douglas S. Duckworth is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar. He earned his BA at James Madison University and his MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later teaching at East Tennessee State University.
Dragana Majhen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed a Master's degree at the University of Manitoba (attested 2010) under thesis advisor Albert Welter.

Dragomir Dimitrov is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn and held posts at Marburg, the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Dramdul is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He was Director at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2007) and editor-in-chief for Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (attested 2013).
Drodul Dorji Tenzin studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Drodul Pawo Dorje studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Ayu Khandro and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Drolkar Chungchung studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Drolma is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Oslo (attested 2008), completing an M. Phil in Tibetan Studies under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik.
Drubwang Shakya Shri studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.
Drukpa Lama Rik Drol Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jampal Delek Nyima and others, and taught Keith Dowman, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, and numerous other students.

Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, founded the International Nyingma Society, and taught students including Matthew T. Kapstein and Alexander Berzin.

Duncan Ryūken Williams specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Reed College and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi, later holding posts at UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.
Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed a PhD at Boston University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Malcolm David Eckel.

Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle (1927–1997) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sera and Gyuto monasteries under Tsadru Ngawang Losang. He held posts at Minzu University of China, Tibet University, and the China Tibetology Research Center.
